hindi: परन्तु जो स्नेह अच्छ रूप में पीने योग्य है, उसे विचारणा नहीं कहते; वह वैद्यों द्वारा देखा गया स्नेह का प्राथमिक कल्प है।
english: But the sneha which is to be drunk plain (accha) they do not call a vicāraṇā; that, recognised by physicians, is the primary mode (kalpa) of sneha.

hindi: जो कल स्नेह पीना चाहता है, उसे द्रव, उष्ण, अनभिष्यन्दी, बहुत स्निग्ध नहीं और असंकीर्ण अन्न उचित मात्रा में खाना चाहिए।
english: By one who wishes to drink fat tomorrow, food that is liquid, warm, not channel-clogging (anabhiṣyandin), not too unctuous and not mixed should be eaten in proper quantity.
notes: asaṃkīrṇa: 'not mixed', i.e. not of many kinds together.

hindi: शमन स्नेह को भोजन के समय भूख लगने पर पिए; परन्तु शोधन के लिए मनुष्य रात्रि का आहार पच जाने पर पिए।
english: One should drink the pacifying fat at meal-time, when hungry; but for purification a man should drink it when the night's meal has been digested.
notes: prakāṃkṣitaḥ: past participle with active sense, 'one who desires (food)'. āhāre naiśe jīrṇe is a locative absolute.

hindi: वह उष्ण जल का उपयोग करने वाला, ब्रह्मचारी और रात में सोने वाला हो, और उत्पन्न हुए मल, मूत्र, अपान वायु और डकार को न रोके।
english: He should use warm water, be celibate and sleep at night, and he should not suppress faeces, urine, flatus and belching when they have arisen.
notes: anila here is flatus. kṣapāśaya: 'sleeping at night' (i.e. not by day).

hindi: व्यायाम, ऊँचे स्वर में बोलना, क्रोध और शोक, शीत और धूप को त्याग दे, और वायु-रहित शय्या और आसन का सेवन करे।
english: He should avoid exercise, loud speaking, anger and grief, cold and sun, and should use a bed and seat sheltered from wind.

words.gram: m. nom. sg. pres. part. mid. prati-√bhuj

hindi: जिस मनुष्य ने स्नेह पिया है और जो स्नेह का प्रतिभोजन कर ही रहा है; क्योंकि स्नेह के मिथ्या उपचार से दारुण रोग उत्पन्न होते हैं।
english: A man who has drunk fat, and who is indeed partaking of fat in turn: for from wrong management of fat dreadful diseases arise.
notes: The first line has no verb; it refers back to the rules of units 62 and 63, and the translations keep it verbless. pratibhuñjānaḥ sneham: literally 'eating fat in return / in turn'; its exact sense (taking fat with food, or after the drink) is not fixed by the line.
lines_deva: स्नेहं पीत्वा नरः स्नेहं प्रतिभुञ्जान एव च
lines_iast: snehaṃ pītvā naraḥ snehaṃ pratibhuñjāna eva ca

hindi: मृदु कोष्ठ वाला मनुष्य अच्छ स्नेह के सेवन से तीन रात में स्निग्ध हो जाता है, परन्तु क्रूर कोष्ठ वाला सात रात में स्निग्ध होता है।
english: A man with a soft bowel becomes oleated in three nights by taking fat plain (accha); but one with a hard bowel becomes oleated in seven nights.

text_flags.why: typo: 'kroṣṭha' has an extra r; the word is krūrakoṣṭha as in units 46, 50 and 68 of this chunk

notes: accha: 'clear, plain', i.e. fat taken by itself, not mixed with food.

hindi: गुड़, गन्ने का रस, मस्तु, दूध, मथा हुआ दही, पायस, कृशरा, घी, काश्मर्य और त्रिफला का रस,
english: Jaggery, sugarcane juice, whey (mastu), milk, churned curd, milk-rice (pāyasa), kṛśarā, ghee, the juice of kāśmarya and triphalā,
notes: Sentence continues into unit 67 (pītvā ... viricyate). kṛśarā: a dish of rice and pulse (standard). kāśmarya: Gmelina arborea (standard). triphalā: 'the three fruits' (āmalakī, harītakī, vibhītakī, standard). ulloḍitam is taken with dadhi; kṣīram stands alone.

hindi: द्राक्षा का रस, पीलु का रस, अथवा गरम जल, या नया मद्य पीकर मृदु कोष्ठ वाला विरेचित हो जाता है।
english: grape (drākṣā) juice, pīlu juice, or hot water, or new wine: having drunk these, one with a soft bowel is purged.
notes: End of the sentence begun in unit 66. pīlu: Salvadora persica (probable). drākṣā: grape, Vitis vinifera (standard).
lines_deva: मद्यं वा तरुणं पीत्वा मृदुकोष्ठो विरिच्यते
lines_iast: madyaṃ vā taruṇaṃ pītvā mṛdukoṣṭho viricyate

hindi: ये क्रूर कोष्ठ वाले का कभी विरेचन नहीं करते; क्रूर कोष्ठ वाले की ग्रहणी अत्यन्त प्रबल अनिल वाली होती है।
english: These never purge one with a hard bowel; the grahaṇī of one with a hard bowel has excessively strong Vāta (anila).
notes: grahaṇī: literally 'the holder', the seat of digestion.

words.gloss: with excited Pitta and little Kapha

hindi: मृदु कोष्ठ वाले व्यक्ति की ग्रहणी में पित्त बढ़ा हुआ, कफ अल्प और मारुत मन्द होता है; इसलिए वह मनुष्य सरलता से विरेचन के योग्य माना गया है।
english: In one with soft bowels (mṛdukoṣṭha) the grahaṇī has excited Pitta, little Kapha and weak Vāta (māruta); therefore that man is regarded as easily purged.
notes: grahaṇī is kept as Sanskrit (seat of digestion). udīrṇapittālpakaphā and mandamārutā are bahuvrīhis agreeing with grahaṇī.
lines_deva: मृदुकोष्ठस्य तस्मात् स सुविरेच्यो नरः स्मृतः
lines_iast: mṛdukoṣṭhasya tasmāt sa suvirecyo naraḥ smṛtaḥ

words.gloss: by the heat of the fire

hindi: जिसकी ग्रहणी में पित्त बढ़ा हुआ हो और जिसका अग्निबल महान् हो, उसका पिया हुआ स्नेह अग्नि के तेज से शीघ्र भस्म हो जाता है।
english: He whose grahaṇī has excited Pitta and whose strength of digestive fire (agni) is great: in him the fat (sneha) that is drunk quickly turns to ash by the heat of the fire.

words.gram: pres. part. caus. pra-√kṣar m. nom. sg.

hindi: वह बलवान स्नेहाग्नि उस स्नेह-मात्रा को खाकर, ओज को बहाती हुई, उपद्रवों सहित अत्यधिक तृष्णा उत्पन्न कर देती है।
english: That strong fire fed by fat (snehāgni), having consumed that dose of fat and causing ojas (vital essence) to flow away, would bring on extreme thirst with complications.
notes: saḥ agrees with snehāgniḥ (m.), the digestive fire intensified by the fat of 70. prakṣārayan is taken as the causative of pra-√kṣar, 'making (ojas) flow away, wasting it'. upasarga = complication, accompanying disorder.

words.gloss: lying in the middle of a thicket
by the fire of its own venom

hindi: स्नेह से बढ़ी हुई (अग्नि) को शान्त करने के लिए अत्यन्त भारी अन्न भी पर्याप्त नहीं होता; यदि उसे अत्यन्त शीतल जल न मिले तो वह जलने लगता है, जैसे झाड़ी के बीच पड़ा विषैला सर्प अपने ही विष की अग्नि से जलता है।
english: Food, even very heavy, is not sufficient to pacify the (fire) increased by fat; if he does not obtain very cold water, he is burnt, just as a venomous snake lying in the middle of a thicket (is burnt) by the fire of its own venom.
notes: snehasamṛddhasya is taken as referring to the snehāgni of 71 ('of the fire increased by fat'); it could also be 'of the man filled with fat'. kakṣa = dry grass, brushwood or thicket. The unit has three printed lines (72a-c) as the edition numbers them.

hindi: यदि स्नेह के न पचने पर तृष्णा हो तो वैद्य वमन कराए; फिर शीतल जल पीकर और रूखा अन्न खाकर (रोगी) उल्लेखन करे।
english: But if thirst arises while the fat is undigested, the physician should make him vomit; then, having drunk cold water and having eaten dry food, (the patient) should vomit.
notes: The subject of ullikhet ('should bring up, vomit') is taken to be the patient; punaḥ may mean 'then' or 'again'.

english: Ghee alone (should) not (be given) in Pitta, especially when it is associated with āma (undigested matter); for it would pervade the whole body and, destroying consciousness, would kill.

hindi: जठर रोग, ग्रहणी दोष, स्तैमित्य, वाणी का रुकना, शूल और आम के दोष — ये स्नेह के अनुचित प्रयोग से उत्पन्न होते हैं।
english: abdominal disease (jaṭhara), grahaṇī disorders, sluggish heaviness (staimitya), obstruction of speech, pain (śūla) and disorders of āma arise from the mishandling of sneha.
notes: Completes the list begun in 75. jaṭhara here = disease of the abdomen (udara). staimitya: a feeling of numb heaviness. vibhrama = error, wrong handling.

hindi: उसमें भी उल्लेखन, स्वेद, समय की प्रतीक्षा, और प्रत्येक बार व्याधि के बल को समझकर स्रंसन भी प्रशस्त है।
english: In that case too, vomiting (ullekhana), sweating (sveda), waiting for time, and also laxative purgation (sraṃsana), after judging the strength of the disease in each case, are recommended.

text_flags.why: tatra + api gives tatrāpi with long ā; the Devanagari also has तत्रप्यु without the ā sign, a typing slip (metre unaffected).

notes: prati prati is read distributively ('case by case', 'according to each').

lines_iast: prati prati vyādhibalaṃ buddhvā sraṃsanameva ca

words.gloss: medicine for the ill effects of sneha

hindi: तक्र और अरिष्ट का प्रयोग, रूखे पेय और अन्न का सेवन, तथा मूत्रों और त्रिफला का (प्रयोग) — यह स्नेह की व्यापत्ति की औषध है।
english: The administration of buttermilk (takra) and ariṣṭa, the taking of dry drinks and food, and (the administration) of urines and of triphalā are the medicine for the ill effects of sneha.
notes: The genitives mūtrāṇām and triphalāyāḥ depend on prayoga understood from line a. ariṣṭa here is the fermented medicinal drink, not 'fatal signs'. triphalā = the three fruits harītakī, vibhītakī and āmalakī: Terminalia chebula, T. bellirica, Phyllanthus emblica (standard).

words.gloss: would go wrong, cause ill effects

hindi: अकाल में, अहितकर, उचित मात्रा में न दिया गया, मिथ्या उपचार से और अति सेवन किया गया स्नेह व्यापत्ति उत्पन्न कर सकता है।
english: Sneha used at the wrong time, unwholesome, not applied in (proper) measure, through wrong management, and used in excess, would go wrong (cause ill effects).
notes: mātrayā na yojitaḥ: 'not applied with measure', i.e. in the wrong dose.
lines_deva: अकाले चाहितश्चैव मात्रया न च योजितः
lines_iast: akāle cāhitaścaiva mātrayā na ca yojitaḥ

hindi: स्नेहन के बाद व्यक्ति तीन रात रुककर, तीन दिन तक स्नेहयुक्त, द्रव और उष्ण मांसरस-भात खाकर, प्रस्कन्दन पिए।
english: After oleation (sneha), the person, having paused for three nights, should drink a purgative (praskandana), after eating for three days boiled rice with meat-juice that is liquid, warm and contains fat.
notes: snehavat, drava and uṣṇa are taken with rasaudanam. snehāt is the ablative with uparataḥ: 'having ceased from oleation for three nights'.

words.gloss: as for one who has been purged

hindi: एक दिन रुककर और उसी प्रकार भोजन करके वह वमनकारक औषध पिए। परन्तु जो स्नेह शोधन के लिए न हो, उसमें चर्या विरेचन किए हुए व्यक्ति के समान हो।
english: Having paused for one day and having eaten likewise, he should drink an emetic. But when the sneha is not meant for purification, the regimen should be as for one who has been purged.
notes: tadvat 'likewise' refers to the food of 80b (liquid, warm, fatty meat-juice with rice).

hindi: जो मनुष्य स्नेह से द्वेष करते हैं, जो नित्य स्नेह लेते हैं, जिनका कोष्ठ मृदु है, जो क्लेश सहन नहीं कर सकते और जो नित्य मद्य पीते हैं, उनके लिए विचारणा इष्ट है।
english: Men who dislike fat, who are habituated to fat, who have soft bowels, who cannot bear hardship and who habitually drink wine: for them vicāraṇā (sneha combined with food) is recommended.

text_flags.why: 'snehavityā' gives no sense; the parallel madyanityāḥ in line b suggests sneha-nityāḥ 'habituated to fat' (व/न confusion), possible typing slip; metre unaffected.

notes: vicāraṇā: giving sneha mixed with food and drink rather than drunk by itself; the following verses (83-89) list such combinations.

words.gloss: of quail, partridge, peacock, swan, boar and cock
of cow, goat, sheep and fish

hindi: लवा, तीतर, मोर, हंस, सूअर, मुर्गा, गाय, बकरी, भेड़ और मछली के मांसरस स्नेहन में हितकर होते हैं।
english: Meat-juices (rasa) of quail, partridge, peacock, swan, boar, cock, cow, goat, sheep and fish are beneficial in oleation.

text_flags.why: āja + aurabhra gives ājaurabhra (a + au = au); the printed 'ājair-' (Devanagari जै for जौ) looks like a slip. The split uses aurabhra. Probable typo.

notes: All members are adjectives of origin (vṛddhi derivatives: taittira from tittiri, aurabhra from urabhra, etc.) agreeing with rasāḥ.

hindi: यव, कोल और कुलत्थ, गुड़ और शर्करा सहित स्नेह, दाड़िम, तथा व्योष सहित दही — यह मांसरस के संयोगों का संग्रह है।
english: Yava, kola and kulattha, fats with jaggery (guḍa) and sugar, dāḍima, and curd with vyoṣa: this is the summary of combinations (saṃyoga) with meat-juice.
notes: savyoṣam may qualify dadhi alone or the whole list. Identifications: yava = barley, Hordeum vulgare (standard); kola = jujube, Ziziphus species (standard); kulattha = horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum, Hindi कुलथी (standard); dāḍima = pomegranate, Punica granatum, Hindi अनार (standard); vyoṣa = the three pungents: dry ginger, black pepper and long pepper (standard).

hindi: पहले खाए गए, स्नेह और फाणित सहित तिल, तथा अधिक स्नेह वाली कृशरा और तिलकाम्बलिका स्नेहन करते हैं।
english: Tila seeds eaten beforehand with fat and phāṇita (treacle) oleate, and so do kṛśarā with much fat and tila-kāmbalikā.
notes: Line b is printed as one unbroken word without spaces; the split is made inside the single token. pūrvam may mean 'before (the meal)'. kṛśarā: rice cooked with pulse; kāmbalikā: kept as Sanskrit. phāṇita: inspissated sugar-cane juice. tila = sesame, Sesamum indicum, Hindi तिल (standard).

hindi: रूक्ष व्यक्ति फाणित, शृङ्गवेर और तेल को सुरा के साथ पिए, और उसके पच जाने पर तैयार किए गए मांसों के साथ भोजन करे।
english: A dry person should drink phāṇita, śṛṅgavera and oil with surā (wine); and when it is digested he should eat a meal with prepared meats.
notes: bhṛtaiḥ (ppp. of √bhṛ 'borne, filled, nourished') is unclear here; 'prepared, cooked' is a guess from context and is marked uncertain. śṛṅgavera = fresh ginger, Zingiber officinale, Hindi अदरक (standard). bhṛtair māṃsaiḥ may also be construed with pibet rather than with bhojanam.
lines_deva: फाणितं शृङ्गवेरं च तैलं च सुरया सह
lines_iast: phāṇitaṃ śṛṅgaveraṃ ca tailaṃ ca surayā saha

hindi: वातिक मनुष्य सुरा के मण्ड के साथ तेल, अथवा वसा या मज्जा, अथवा फाणित सहित दूध पीता हुआ स्निग्ध हो जाता है।
english: A man of Vāta nature (vātika) becomes oleated by drinking oil with the clear upper part (maṇḍa) of surā, or muscle-fat or marrow, or milk with phāṇita.
notes: surāyā maṇḍena may go with tailam only or with vasā and majjā as well. vātika: one in whom Vāta predominates or one suffering from Vāta.
lines_deva: तैलं सुराया मण्डेन वसां मज्जानमेव वा
पिबन् सफाणितं क्षीरं नरः स्निह्यति वातिकः
lines_iast: tailaṃ surāyā maṇḍena vasāṃ majjānameva vā
piban saphāṇitaṃ kṣīraṃ naraḥ snihyati vātikaḥ

hindi: धारोष्ण, स्नेहयुक्त और शर्करा सहित दूध पीकर, अथवा फाणित सहित दही का सर पीकर मनुष्य स्निग्ध हो जाता है।
english: A man becomes oleated by drinking milk warm from the milking, mixed with fat and with sugar, or by drinking the upper layer (sara) of curd with phāṇita.
notes: dhāroṣṇa: milk still warm as it streams from the udder.
lines_deva: नरः स्निह्यति पीत्वा वा सरं दध्नः सफाणितम्
lines_iast: naraḥ snihyati pītvā vā saraṃ dadhnaḥ saphāṇitam

hindi: पाँच प्रसृत वाली पेया, तथा माष मिला, दूध में पकाया हुआ और अधिक स्नेह वाला पायस मनुष्य को शीघ्र स्निग्ध करता है।
english: Thin gruel (peyā) of five prasṛtas, and milk-rice (pāyasa) mixed with māṣa, cooked in milk and with much fat, would quickly oleate a man.
notes: kṣīrasiddha and bahusneha are taken with pāyasa. prasṛta is kept as a measure; 90a states what the five prasṛtas are. māṣa = black gram, Vigna mungo, Hindi उड़द (standard).

words.gloss: with prasṛtas of ghee, oil, muscle-fat, marrow and rice
words.gram: m. inst. pl. tat-puruṣa with dvandva
m. nom. sg. tat-puruṣa with dvandva

hindi: घी, तेल, वसा, मज्जा और चावल के प्रसृतों से पकाई गई पाँच प्रसृत वाली पेया स्नेहन चाहने वाले को पीनी चाहिए। अथवा घी और लवण से युक्त स्निग्ध सूअर का मांसरस दिन में दो बार यत्नपूर्वक पिया जाए तो मनुष्य को शीघ्र स्निग्ध करता है।
english: Thin gruel of five prasṛtas, cooked with prasṛtas of ghee, oil, muscle-fat, marrow and rice, is to be drunk by one who desires oleation. Or unctuous pork meat-juice combined with ghee and salt, drunk carefully twice in a day, would quickly oleate a man.
notes: GROUPING: lines a-b are verse 90; lines c-d are a separate verse printed inside round brackets (probably marking an added or doubtful verse), grouped here under 90 as the edition numbers it; they would better form their own unit (90.1). The printed 'śṛ(kṛ)tā' gives śṛtā with kṛtā in brackets as an alternative; the split follows śṛtā, and both readings give 'cooked/made'. The five prasṛtas of 89a are the five ingredients of line a. Line d repeats the close of 89b.

words.gram: n. acc. sg. adjectival dvandva qualifying māṃsam

hindi: कुष्ठी, शोथी और प्रमेही स्नेहन में ग्राम्य, आनूप और औदक मांस, गुड़, दही, दूध और तिल का प्रयोग न करे।
english: One with kuṣṭha, with swelling (śotha) or with prameha should not use, in oleation, the meat of domestic, marsh and aquatic animals, jaggery (guḍa), curd, milk or tila seeds.
notes: grāmya-ānūpa-audaka is an adjectival compound qualifying māṃsam ('domestic-marsh-aquatic meat').
lines_deva: कुष्ठी शोथी प्रमेही च स्नेहने न प्रयोजयेत्
lines_iast: kuṣṭhī śothī pramehī ca snehane na prayojayet

hindi: उन्हें यथायोग्य, विकार न करने वाले, पिप्पली और हरीतकी से सिद्ध, अथवा त्रिफला से भी सिद्ध स्नेहों द्वारा स्निग्ध करे।
english: He should oleate them, as appropriate, with fats that cause no disorder, prepared with pippalī and harītakī, or also prepared with triphalā.
notes: tān refers to the patients of 91b (those with kuṣṭha, śotha, prameha). Identifications: pippalī = long pepper, Piper longum, Hindi पीपर (पिप्पली) (standard); harītakī = Terminalia chebula, Hindi हरड़ (standard).

words.gloss: with the juices of drākṣā and āmalaka
words.gram: m. inst. du. tat-puruṣa with dvandva

hindi: वैद्य द्राक्षा और आमलक के यूष तथा खट्टे दही से व्योष डालकर स्नेह सिद्ध करे; उसे पीकर मनुष्य स्निग्ध हो जाता है।
english: The physician should prepare fat with vyoṣa inside it, with the juices (yūṣa) of drākṣā and āmalaka and with sour curd; drinking it, a man becomes oleated.
notes: vyoṣagarbha: with vyoṣa (the three pungents) inside it. Identifications: drākṣā = grape, Vitis vinifera (standard); āmalaka = Indian gooseberry, Phyllanthus emblica, Hindi आँवला (standard).
lines_deva: व्योषगर्भं भिषक् स्नेहं पीत्वा स्निह्यति तं नरः
lines_iast: vyoṣagarbhaṃ bhiṣak snehaṃ pītvā snihyati taṃ naraḥ

hindi: यव, कोल और कुलत्थ के रस, क्षार, सुरा, दही, तथा दूध और घी — इनसे सिद्ध वह घी स्नेहन के लिए उत्तम घृत है।
english: The juices of yava, kola and kulattha, alkali (kṣāra), surā, curd, and milk and ghee: that (ghee) prepared (with these) is the best ghee for oleation.
notes: kṣīrasarpiḥ is taken as a samāhāra dvandva 'milk and ghee'; it could also be a tat-puruṣa 'ghee from milk'. tat siddham is taken as the ghee cooked with the listed liquids. For the plants see 84.

words.gloss: with juices of badara and triphalā
words.gram: m. inst. pl. tat-puruṣa with dvandva

words.gloss: in disorders of the yoni and semen
words.gram: m. loc. pl. tat-puruṣa with dvandva

hindi: योनि और शुक्र के दोषों में तेल, मज्जा, वसा और घी को बदर और त्रिफला के रसों से सिद्ध करके प्रयोग करे।
english: In disorders of the yoni (female genital tract) and of semen, one should prepare oil, marrow, muscle-fat and ghee with the juices of badara and triphalā, and use (them).
notes: badara = jujube, Ziziphus species, Hindi बेर (standard); triphalā: see 78.

words.gloss: in proportion to the digestive fire

hindi: जैसे वस्त्र जल को ग्रहण करता है और अधिक को बहा देता है, वैसे ही स्नेह अग्नि के अनुसार पचता है और अधिक (स्नेह) बह जाता है।
english: As cloth takes in water and lets the excess flow out, so fat is digested in proportion to the digestive fire, and the excess flows out.

hindi: अथवा जैसे मिट्टी के पिण्ड को बिना भिगोए उस पर जल्दी से डाला गया जल बह जाता है, वैसे ही जल्दी-जल्दी सेवन किया गया स्नेह निकल जाता है।
english: Or, as water poured hastily on a lump of clay without moistening it runs off, so fat taken hastily slips out.
notes: vākledya is split vā + akledya (negated absolutive of the causative of √klid, 'without wetting'); sravati belongs to the water of line a, sraṃsate to the fat. Alternatively vā + ākledya (abs. caus. ā-√klid, 'having (only) moistened' the clod), the grammatically regular form; a negated absolutive in -ya is irregular.

hindi: लवण मिले स्नेह मनुष्य को शीघ्र स्निग्ध करते हैं, क्योंकि वह (लवण) अभिष्यन्दी, अरूक्ष, सूक्ष्म, उष्ण और व्यवायी है।
english: Fats combined with salt oleate a man quickly, for it (salt) is abhiṣyandin (causing moistening), not dry, subtle, hot and vyavāyin (spreading through the body).
notes: tat (n.) refers to lavaṇa (salt). abhiṣyandin: causing oozing or moistening; vyavāyin: pervading, spreading through the body.

words.gloss: of one who has undergone oleation and sweating
words.gram: m. gen. sg. tat-puruṣa with dvandva

hindi: पहले स्नेह का प्रयोग करे, उसके बाद तुरन्त स्वेद; स्नेह और स्वेद से युक्त व्यक्ति का संशोधन, फिर अन्य (उपचार) करे।
english: One should apply oleation (sneha) first, then, immediately after, sweating (sveda); for one who has undergone oleation and sweating, purification (saṃśodhana), then the other (measure).
notes: itarat 'the other' is not specified in the line; it may mean the other kind of treatment besides purification. atha 'then' is taken as ordering purification before the other measure.

hindi: यहाँ श्लोक है:
english: Here, the verse:
notes: Lead-in of the closing summary verse (100); singular, one verse follows.

words.gloss: the complete successful treatment of ill effects

hindi: स्नेह, स्नेह-विधि, औषधों सहित सम्पूर्ण व्यापत्-सिद्धि — (यह सब) प्रश्नों के अनुसार भगवान् चान्द्रभागि द्वारा कहा गया।
english: The fats, the method of oleation, and the complete success (siddhi) over ill effects together with medicines: (all this) was declared, according to the questions, by the venerable Cāndrabhāgi.
notes: vyāhṛtam (n. sg.) sums up the listed topics. kṛtsna may qualify the whole list ('in full'). cāndrabhāginā: inst. of cāndrabhāgi (i-stem) or cāndrabhāgin; a metronymic epithet 'descendant of Candrabhāgā', kept as an epithet in the translation; it refers to the teacher of the work, whose name the line does not give.

hindi: इस प्रकार अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित और चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र के श्लोकस्थान में स्नेहाध्याय नामक तेरहवाँ अध्याय।
english: Thus, in the Śloka section (Ślokasthāna) of the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, the thirteenth chapter, named Snehādhyāya (Chapter on Sneha).
notes: Chapter colophon; the Sanskrit has no verb and the translation keeps it verbless.
lines_deva: इत्यग्निवेशकृते तन्त्रे चरकप्रतिसंस्कृते श्लोकस्थाने स्नेहाध्यायो नाम त्रयोदशोऽध्यायः
lines_iast: ityagniveśakṛte tantre carakapratisaṃskṛte ślokasthāne snehādhyāyo nāma trayodaśo'dhyāyaḥ
